headline: Red Sox shut out in Bronx as offense stays ice cold
morning_brew: Friday morning feels like a massive hangover after watching that lineup go completely silent in the Bronx. We managed just five hits and zero runs against the Yankees in a game that felt like a funeral procession for our bats. I watched every pitch through my fingers, just waiting for someone to drive a ball into the gap, but it never happened. It is absolutely infuriating to watch us get blanked like that when every win is supposed to matter so much this time of year.

Sandoval gave us a gritty start by going into the sixth, but he takes the loss because he had zero margin for error with the way our hitters were swinging. The bullpen actually looked respectable, putting up scoreless work to keep us within striking distance, but our hitters just could not capitalize when the moment arrived. My mother watched the final three innings and just shook her head before walking out of the room. She has been watching this team for decades and even she looked like she had seen enough of the struggling offense.

Now we have to regroup for a long day of baseball ahead. It is a grind, but we have to find a way to manufacture some runs if we want to stay in the mix. I trust the guys to bounce back because they have shown us flashes of fight before, but we need to stop the bleeding and get some production at the plate. Fenway isn't gonna be happy if we don't start putting up crooked numbers, so it is time to turn the page and get after it.

trend_watch.dans_take: He was the only one showing any signs of life at the plate while everyone else took a nap.

trend_watch.dans_take: He came in and threw strikes, which is more than I can say for the black holes in the lineup.
We need our veteran presence to set the tone, not pull a vanishing act when it matters most.
